evidence.proved: OVHcloud publishes a first-party REST API for MX Plan that lists and manages email accounts
evidence.quote: List email accounts. Returns the email addresses of the email accounts of the service. Filter them by `primaryEmailAddress` or `id`.

reason: the vendor's own developer reference documents a REST API at /v1/email/mxplan/{service}/account using Bearer-token authentication; browser is kept for the documented Roundcube/Zimbra/OWA webmail; the interface vocabulary has no IMAP, POP or SMTP term, so unknown is retained as the nearest term and those protocols are named in interface_detail

old: webmail from a browser, and an email client over IMAP (imap.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net, port 993, SSL/TLS), POP (pop.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net, port 995, SSL/TLS) and SMTP (smtp.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net, port 465, SSL/TLS) in the Europe and Africa zone
new: IMAP, POP and SMTP are documented on the MX Plan: incoming IMAP at imap.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net (port 993, SSL/TLS), incoming POP at pop.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net (port 995, SSL/TLS) and outgoing SMTP at smtp.mail.ovh.net or ssl0.ovh.net (port 465, SSL/TLS). Webmail is available from a browser (Roundcube, Zimbra or OWA, depending on the service). OVHcloud also publishes a first-party REST management API for MX Plan at /v1/email/mxplan/{service}/account with Bearer-token authentication, covering listing, creating, updating and deleting mailboxes and changing passwords; it manages the service and is not a message-access protocol. No JMAP endpoint or JMAP support is listed on the first-party MX Plan guides, the email FAQ or the developer reference pages read. The interface vocabulary has no term for IMAP, POP, SMTP or JMAP, so unknown is kept as the nearest term for those protocols.
